name.title: Hey! What would you like to call me?
name.lede: Pick any name you like. It is also my wake word: say it out loud, and I'm listening. You can change it anytime in Settings.
name.label: Assistant name
name.owner_label: And what should I call you? (optional)
name.local_note: These names stay on this computer. They are not sent to any AI engine.

connect.title: Connect your AI
connect.lede: Sign in with a subscription you already pay for, or paste an API key. One of them is enough for {name} to think and talk.
connect.finish_in_browser: Finish the sign-in in your browser.
connect.install_first: Install it first: run this in a terminal, then check again.
connect.key_partial: Some parts did not switch ({parts}). You can fix them later on the API Keys page.
connect.live_ready: Live voice is on: talk, and {name} answers right away.
connect.live_missing: Chat works. Live voice needs an OpenAI or Gemini key; until then {name} speaks the classic way, a little slower.
connect.key_security: Subscriptions are billed at a flat monthly price. Keys go into your system's keychain and only ever to the provider you picked.
connect.nothing_yet: Nothing connected yet. Without a subscription or a key, chat and voice stay off. You can connect one later on the API Keys page.
connect.one_first: Set up one engine first. Comparing several engines comes later, in Settings.
connect.kinds_note: An engine can run on this computer (local), through an API key you pay for by use, or through an official sign-in with your subscription. A subscription is not API credit, and none of them is checked until you use it.
connect.work_lede: Jarvis Work only uses engines that run on this computer.
connect.work_local_only: Nothing here is sent to the cloud, and nothing falls back to a cloud engine.
connect.work_need: If no local engine is ready you can still explore the interface. The chat cannot answer until one is installed; nothing is downloaded for you.

voice.title: How you'll talk to {name}
voice.lede: Type in the chat, or just speak: say your wake word, or press your Call shortcut.
voice.call_detail: Press it anywhere to start talking. Click the keys to choose your own.
voice.call_recording: Hold the keys you want, then let go. Esc cancels.
voice.call_none: No shortcut yet. Click the field and press the keys you want.
voice.call_saved: Saved. Press it anywhere to start talking.
voice.call_refused: This combination can't be used. Try another one.
voice.wake_on: Always listening for your wake word. It is recognised right here on this computer.
voice.wake_off: Off: press your Call shortcut to talk. Turn it on to have your wake word heard all the time.
voice.wake_switch: Always listen for the wake word
voice.after_restart: This switches on with the restart at the end.
voice.login_detail: Opens {name} when your computer starts, so it is ready to hear you.
voice.preview_note: This is a replay, so nothing restarts.
voice.restart_note: Next, a short walk shows you around the app. At the end the app restarts once (about ten seconds) to switch everything on.
voice.mode_label: How do you want to talk to me?
voice.mode_text_hint: Type in the chat. Always available.
voice.mode_voice_hint: Speak instead. Your computer asks for the microphone the first time you use it.
voice.mode_both_hint: Type or speak, whichever suits the moment.
voice.mic_note: Text always stays available. Nothing here turns the microphone on, and no voice test is required.

tour.title: A walk through {name}
tour.lede: Your pet walks you through the app and explains each section.

stops.chat: Hi, I'm {pet}! Let me show you around. This is your chat with {name}. Type anything here: a question, a task, a file to look at. You never pick a tool or a model yourself; {name} decides what's needed.
stops.voice: Rather talk? This is voice chat. Click the bar, say your wake word or press your Call shortcut, then just speak. The wave shows who is talking.
stops.agents: Big jobs like research, a report or a website go to your agents. They're {name}'s team, each with its own role and model. Open Agents to watch them work, chat with one or create your own.
stops.ide: The Agentic IDE runs coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in real terminals, on your own projects. Type to them directly, or let {name} steer them by voice.
stops.plugins: Plugins connect {name} to the apps you use: mail, calendar, notes, smart home and more. Each one becomes a new tool, and anything that sends or changes something asks you first.
stops.wake: Your wake word lives here in Settings. Say "Hey {name}" and {name} listens. Change the word, pick its language or test it anytime.
stops.done: That's the tour! Talk to {name} whenever you like, and if you're ever stuck, just ask. Settings → App runs this guide again.

personality.title: How should I sound?
personality.lede: Pick a style, or skip it: you can change it anytime in your profile.
personality.friendly_sample: Happy to help! Tell me what you have in mind and we'll sort it out together.
personality.ironic_sample: Sure, I'll help. I'll even keep the jokes to a socially acceptable level.
personality.essential_sample: Tell me what you need. I'll answer briefly and to the point.
personality.professional_sample: Understood. Please share the details and I will prepare a clear answer.
personality.collaborative_sample: Good, let's work through it together. What is the goal, and what do we already have?
personality.sample_note: These are written examples, not answers from an AI.
personality.tone_label: Should I keep this tone or adapt it?
personality.tone_keep_hint: I stay as you set me. Nothing shifts by itself.
personality.tone_adapt: Adapt the tone to the situation
personality.tone_adapt_hint: Small, temporary shifts within the style you chose. You can turn it off anytime.
personality.simulated: My mood is simulated: a way of speaking, not a feeling. It never changes facts, permissions, privacy, budget or approvals.

privacy.title: Privacy and actions
privacy.lede: What stays here, and what I will ask you first.
privacy.consumer_local: Your main memory stays on this computer.
privacy.consumer_remote: If you connect a cloud engine, it receives the part of a conversation that is sent to it. You are told what, before you connect one.
privacy.work_local: Your data is processed by engines on this computer.
privacy.work_offline: Running locally is not the same as fully offline. Under the strict offline profile, features without verified enforcement are unavailable.
privacy.memory_off: Off: I will not save notes about you until you turn this on.
privacy.memory_on: On: I may keep short notes about you and our work. You can read and delete them.
privacy.actions_body: I ask for your approval before acting. Finishing this guide gives me no access to your files, email, browser, tools or services; each of those asks separately.

summary.title: Your Jarvis
summary.lede: This is what is set right now.
summary.engine_state_local_server_not_checked: selected; the local server was not checked
summary.engine_state_not_verified_with_a_request: connected; not verified with a request
summary.memory_off: Ask first: learning is off until you turn it on
summary.actions_other: Does not ask every time (change it in Settings)
summary.ready_consumer: I'm ready. Would you like to introduce yourself, or shall we start with something you're interested in?
summary.ready_work: Which project shall we start with? An empty project is fine; nothing is scanned or imported.
summary.not_ready: The engine is not ready, so the chat cannot answer yet. You can explore the interface and connect one later.
summary.preview_note: This is a replay: nothing was changed.
summary.unavailable: The summary is not available right now.

app_tour.replay_body: Opens the setup window again (name, AI connections, voice), then the walk through the app. Nothing restarts.
